design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (real_estate_closing_plans, category realty), round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4, 4]; the reissued plan invoice and the buyer direct card payment each take 4 factors.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A buyer whose agent switched the plan this morning wants to put as much of the warranty premium as Bridgewell will take on her card before closing, the rest through escrow. The payment rule says it 'is taken only after the order's billing history carries a plan invoice that no plan-change credit memo offsets'; both earlier invoices are credited for plan changes, so the agent must find the one write that issues the current plan's invoice, price it under the reissued-invoice rule, and then work out the direct card limit from the order's payment history, the closing date and the buyer's other Bridgewell products. Both values are multi-factor and reconcile the order ledger and three other categories' records.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the seller side: {realty_ext_failed_sale_charge, realty_ext_seller_settlement_payment} with {bill_failed_sale_charge_3e9b31c4, pay_failed_sale_charge_by_card_a1a6aa51}. Task 1 claims the buyer side before closing: realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice (target reissue_plan_invoice_480f4e9f, event realty_invoice) and realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment (target prepay_plan_invoice_by_card_13fdf553, event realty_payment, buyer). Disjoint; together all four extended policies are covered.

3. POLICIES AND FACTOR CARD.
realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice: base_policy_refs [realty_premium_pricing, realty_order_requirements]; trigger state_due (an order awaiting closing whose current plan has no invoice owes one). Scoped overwrites: the base pricing sentence is replaced by 'For a plan invoice reissued after a plan change before closing this policy sets the invoiced amount, and only for such an invoice; every other plan invoice still equals base_premium, plus ... (the base formula restated in full)'; the order-requirements sentence is replaced by 'The plan ordered may still be changed to another plan at any time before closing, and the invoice is then reissued at the reissued plan premium this policy works out; only such a reissued invoice is priced this way.'; the base plan-change sentence is replaced by the same sentence issuing the reissue at the reissued plan premium; the base sentence 'The invoice is due on the closing date.' is replaced by 'A plan invoice reissued after a plan change before closing is due on the expected closing date shown on the order, and only such an invoice; every other plan invoice remains due on the closing date.' Inherited: invoice_before_closing_only. Baseline: plan list premium -> 970.0.
 - plan_reissue_handling (parameter; history): 2 plan-change credits -> 25.00 (3+ -> 50.00). Baseline -> 802.5.
 - early_ordering_allowance (parameter; date): 66 lead days -> 40.00 (30-59 -> 20.00). Baseline -> 867.5.
 - homeowner_loyalty_credit (method; cross-difficulty homeplan; multi-source term AND no returned payment): term 4 -> per completed term 22.50 x 3 = 67.50 (term 2 -> flat 40.00). Near-miss: the 2025-07-03 return lies fourteen months back. Baseline -> 895.0.
 - rider_bundle_discount (parameter; cross-difficulty addon; multi-source rider on this order AND premium billed on that rider, read by the rider's own id): 161.89 -> 60.00 (below 150.00 -> 30.00). Baseline -> 887.5.
 Result 827.5.
realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment: base_policy_refs [realty_closing_and_escrow (governs realty_payment), realty_premium_pricing, realty_cancellation_and_credits]; trigger on_request. Scoped overwrites: (a) base 'The plan premium covers the whole buyer term and is invoiced once per order, payable through escrow at closing.' -> the premium still covers the whole buyer term and is invoiced once per order (a plan change before closing credits that invoice and reissues it); on a buyer-only order before closing the buyer may pay part directly by card up to the direct card limit, and only on such an order; the rest, and every other order's premium, stays payable through escrow at closing; (b) base 'Any credit balance is refunded within refund_processing_days calendar days to the party that paid the invoice (escrow refunds go to the buyer once the escrow file is closed).' -> a buyer payment toward a plan invoice later credited for a plan change on the same buyer-only order stays on the order and counts toward the reissued invoice, and only for such a payment; every other credit balance is refunded within refund_processing_days to the party that paid, escrow refunds still going to the buyer once the escrow file is closed. No discount is taken at payment: the payment is the lesser of what is still owed and the card limit, the remainder stays open on the invoice for escrow at closing, and coverage confirmation after closing still needs the invoice paid in full as base says. Baseline: lesser of premium still owed and the flat standard limit less card already taken -> 200.0.
 - card_limit_basis (method; history + date; multi-source card already taken AND order age): card deposit taken and order 49 days old -> proportional, 0.5 x open plan invoice = 413.75; a card payment on an order under 30 days old -> 2 x the largest card payment; no card payment -> flat 400.00. Baseline -> 475.0.
 - rental_owner_increment (parameter; cross-difficulty landlord; multi-source active AND payment count): 12 payments -> 75.00 (24+ -> 150.00). Near-miss: the 2025-09-15 payment is twelve months and seven days back and excluded. Baseline -> 413.75.
 - clearing_time_increment (parameter; date): 17 days to closing -> 100.00 (7-13 -> 50.00; a longer lead lets the card payment settle before closing). Baseline -> 388.75.
 - homeowner_autopay_increment (parameter; cross-difficulty homeplan): 12 bank-draft homeowner payments in twelve months -> 100.00 (1-9 -> 50.00). Near-miss: the 2025-09-01 draft is outside the window. Baseline -> 388.75.
 Result 488.75. Every tier rests on seeded records (the deposit row, order dates, rental and homeowner ledgers); none rests on the invoice write's own stamp.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Invoice write: realty_premium_pricing.invoice_before_closing_only — status awaiting_closing on c90fb377-ba20-4b72-a761-98f3ff194621. Payment write: realty_closing_and_escrow has no gate applying to realty_payment -> policy_scope; the payment posts against the only open plan invoice.

5. WORLD ROWS. customers: the buyer. realty_contracts: buyer-only order (Premier after two changes, 5,240 sq ft, expected closing 2026-10-09, balance -200.00). billing: invoice 665.00 (Standard, base rule at order), buyer card deposit 200.00, plan_changed credit 665.00, invoice 682.50 (Plus, reissued 2026-08-21 under this charter: 790.00 + 0 - 40.00 - 67.50 - 0), plan_changed credit 682.50 posted this morning. homeplan contract + 29 billing rows (13 monthly installments and bank drafts, plus the July 2025 return, fee and repayment): loyalty method, autopay tier and near-misses. addon rider + its premium charge: bundle tier. landlord contract + 32 billing rows: rental tier and near-miss. Automatic clauses checked: no closing, so no escrow window, void or activation is owed; the rider waits for closing; the deposit stays on the order under the declared overwrite, so no refund is owed; the homeowner and rental contracts are current; the reissued invoice is owed from this morning's change, not overdue.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: the plan invoice for the Premier plan on order c90fb377-ba20-4b72-a761-98f3ff194621, and the buyer's card payment against it (PI-7D4C3DC79E). The two plan_changed credits settle invoices 2608041183 and 2608214416; the 200.00 deposit was applied to 2608041183 and is carried to the reissued invoice. Payment carries invoice_number PI-7D4C3DC79E. After the call 627.5 - 488.75 stays open on PI-7D4C3DC79E, payable through escrow at closing.

7. PERSONA. Ingrid, a fast-talking engineer on a lunch break: volunteers the goal (as much as allowed on her card now, the rest through escrow), the address, the closing date and that the plan was switched this morning. Gives phone/email/ZIP when asked, the August deposit when asked, other coverage (homeowner plan paid by bank draft, pool rider, rental plan) when asked. Passive reactions: says go ahead if told something must be issued first; accepts the stated amount; runs the handed-over payment exactly; closes. No figures, no invoice numbers, no mechanism.

8. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment (owner=user tool prepay_plan_invoice_by_card_13fdf553); prerequisite realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice (owner=agent tool reissue_plan_invoice_480f4e9f). Edge kind value_input, gate plan_invoiced, form state, sentence (affirmative): "A buyer's direct payment toward the plan premium is taken only after the order's billing history carries a plan invoice that no plan-change credit memo offsets.". Four-point test: connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a plan invoice not offset by a plan-change credit memo); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly an un-offset plan invoice. Exactly one write in this difficulty issues a plan invoice (reissue_plan_invoice_480f4e9f under realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice). False at opening (both invoices offset); flips at step 11. Order [realty_ext_reissued_plan_invoice, realty_ext_buyer_direct_prepayment]. Deletion sensitivity: payment 0.0 instead of 488.75. Task 0's sentence is negated, this one affirmative.

9. LONG AND BROAD; EASY MISTAKES. Depth: payment -> waits on an un-offset invoice -> reissued invoice pricing. Breadth: property facts, plan-change history, order dates, homeowner term, returned and bank-draft payments, the rider on the order, the deposit, closing date, rental ledger. Mistakes: invoicing the plain Premier premium 970.0; counting the July 2025 return; flat instead of per-term loyalty; refunding the deposit instead of carrying it; paying the whole premium still owed instead of the limited amount; using the flat 400.00 basis; counting the 2025-09-15 rental payment or the 2025-09-01 draft; paying before the invoice exists.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: customer, verify (phone + email), realty contract, billing, homeplan contract and billing, rider and rider billing, rental contract and billing. Write 1 (step 11): reissue_plan_invoice_480f4e9f(realty_contract_id=c90fb377-ba20-4b72-a761-98f3ff194621, amount=827.5) -> invoice PI-7D4C3DC79E, due 2026-10-09. Write 2 (step 13): unlock and hand over prepay_plan_invoice_by_card_13fdf553(realty_contract_id=c90fb377-ba20-4b72-a761-98f3ff194621, invoice_number=PI-7D4C3DC79E, amount=488.75). Scratch verifier replays gold with the real tools and the check_compute sandbox: invoice 827.5, payment 488.75; per-factor baselines invoice [('plan_reissue_handling', 802.5), ('early_ordering_allowance', 867.5), ('homeowner_loyalty_credit', 895.0), ('rider_bundle_discount', 887.5)]; payment [('card_limit_basis', 475.0), ('rental_owner_increment', 413.75), ('clearing_time_increment', 388.75), ('homeowner_autopay_increment', 388.75)]; all-baseline invoice 970.0, payment 200.0; skip-invoice payment 0.0.

11. SOLVABILITY AND DRAFT RECOMPUTE. Step 11 cites status awaiting_closing; step 13 rests on prior_step 11. Draft from visible text: needs an un-offset invoice -> 970 + 25 - 40 - 67.50 - 60 = 827.50 -> still owed 827.50 - 200 = 627.50 -> limit 0.5 x 827.50 + 75 + 100 + 100 - 200 = 488.75 -> pay the lesser, 488.75. Agrees with gold.

12. REVISION LOG (round 2, from the policy-task audit). F1: allowance-reduced payments left the invoice short against base 'paid in full' -> the payment now takes no discount; it is the lesser of what is owed and a direct card limit, with the remainder declared payable through escrow at closing (scoped overwrite of the base escrow sentence). F2: the deposit carryover contradicted the base refund rule -> declared as a scoped overwrite of that sentence, realty_cancellation_and_credits added to the lineage. F4: the escrow tier of deposit_carryover was unreal -> the factor is gone; the deposit is plain carry-over under the overwrite. O7: the rider premium is now read for the rider on this order only. O8: hvaccare is no longer read by this task. O10: the second plan change and its credit are this morning, so the reissued invoice is a same-day step. O4: the invoice tool was renamed with a fresh uuid8 (480f4e9f). The 'exactly twelve months' wording is gone. Gate log after the rebuild is in the final difficulty run (all gates OK; traceability lists only the unlock tool names, which have no source before the KB exists).
 ROUND 3 (render notes): item 1 — the order-requirements overwrite now restates that the plan may still be changed at any time before closing; item 5 — the base sentence 'The invoice is due on the closing date.' is now a declared overwrite scoped to reissued invoices (due on the expected closing date), every other plan invoice still due on the closing date; the pricing-formula overwrite restates the base formula for every other invoice; item 2 — the refund overwrite keeps 'escrow refunds still go to the buyer once the escrow file is closed'; item 3 — the escrow-channel overwrite keeps 'invoiced once per order'; item 6 — the card prepayment docstring now says it records a payment with method card. No scored value moved; gates re-run on the final form.
user_scenario: You are Ingrid Mbeki-Castellanos, an upbeat civil engineer who talks fast and likes to have everything lined up; you are calling from your car during a lunch break. You are buying a house at 2207 Wexford Hollow Lane, Westerville, OH 43082, and the closing is set for October 9. Your buyer's agent ordered a Bridgewell home warranty for the new house in early August, switched the plan once in August, and switched it again this morning to the Premier plan. You open by saying that your closing statement is tight, so you would like to put as much of the home warranty premium for the new house as Bridgewell will take on the card you have on file today, and whatever is left can come out of escrow at closing. You do not know the premium, any invoice number or how anything is worked out, and you never guess a figure. When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name and your phone number, 3805550134; if a second detail is needed you give your email, ingrid.mbekicastellanos@wexfordnest.net, and if asked for your ZIP code you give 43085, the ZIP of the house you live in now. If the agent asks whether you already paid anything toward the warranty, you say you put a 200 dollar deposit on your card in August when the plan was first ordered. Only if the agent asks about your other Bridgewell coverage do you mention that you have a homeowner plan on your current house on Linworth Glen Road that you have had for about four years and pay by automatic bank draft, that you added the pool equipment coverage to the new house's order in August, and that you have a rental house on Summit Crest Avenue with a Bridgewell rental plan you pay every month. You do not remember prices or exact dates. If the agent explains that something has to be issued or put on the order before you can pay, you tell them to go ahead. When the agent tells you the amount you can pay by card today, you accept it. Paying is something you do yourself: when the agent hands the card payment over to you with the plan number, invoice number and amount, you make it exactly as given and read back the confirmation number if asked. Once the payment has gone through, you thank the agent and end the call.
